text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS

- Deputy Prime Minister Francisco Alvarez Cascos says former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez and his friends orchestrated 1980s campaign by self-styled Anti-terrorist Liberation Groups (GAL) against Basque separatists.
- Basque regional government opens way for job-sharing with subsidies to firms.
EL MUNDO
- Military intelligence service CESID filmed private meetings between top officials in luxury chalet.
- Barca wins in Zaragoza amid scandal.
DIARIO 16
- Secretary of State for Social Security Juan Carlos Aparicio says pension reform will be gradual and moderate.
ABC
- ABC enters computer of Moncloa presidential complex.
- State will earn more than 500 billion pesetas from privatisation of Repsol and Telefonica.
CINCO DIAS
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar delays hard budgetary adjustment in favour of social cohesion; creative accounting is tolerated to reach Euro goal.
- Tax bureau alarmed by public works spending.
EXPANSION
- Aznar says Spain will be be among first single currency group (joint interview with Financial Times).
- Head of stock exchange commission CNMV says state can guarantee independence of some firms.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Iberdrola and Telefonica reconsider their alliance in telecommunications.
- One and a half million Latin Americans entrust their pension to Spanish banks.
- Banco Santander and businessman Juan Abello create investors' club.
